messages.content: Ongoing: RoboRide drops price to $0.12 per mile. Wait time now 8 minutes. Coverage expanded to residential areas. Partnership wit
You notice more robotaxis on the streets. About 7% of people seem to be using them regularly.
People around you are stressed: Tom Bradley, Betty Kowalski. The mood is tense.

Dale called Lisa Freeman directly and got the answer he needed: the drainage and waterproofing bid on the Elm Street property is moving forward — the owner, a retired teacher named Harold Grant, had been waiting on a relative's opinion and got it this week, and he wants Dale to start within two weeks. The second bid (a fence and grading project) remains stalled and Lisa is treating it as cold. More significantly, Lisa confirmed the community center has a failing section of flat roof over the annex — she is bringing Dale's name to the board this week with a nonprofit rate conversation in mind. Carlos Ruiz took the referral ask without any awkwardness and mentioned a property on Concord Lane whose owner has been asking around about basement waterproofing — he promised to pass the name along. Two new bids went out for essential-repair work: roofing on a duplex flagged by a former client, and drainage grading for a residential property near the creek corridor.
